entryPoint.startedFrom: https://www.longines.com/ (redirected by browser default locale to https://www.longines.com/zh-tw)
entryPoint.resolvedViaCountrySelector: Clicked/confirmed the site's own language/country navigation link labelled 'Deutschland' -> https://www.longines.com/de
entryPoint.note: https://www.longines.com/de-de/watches returned a 'Page not found' (404-style SPA page); the site's actual German-market path is https://www.longines.com/de/watches (no region suffix), confirmed only after opening the real country selector menu and reading the rendered 'Deutschland' link href, not guessed.

networkDiscovery.notes: Used Chrome DevTools MCP (mcp__chrome-devtools__*). Captured live network requests on https://www.longines.com/de/watches and on its 'Mehr Ergebnisse anzeigen' (load-more) interaction, identified the underlying Magento-style GraphQL endpoint https://www.longines.com/api/graphql with operationName=ProductList (reqid 427), and replayed the identical query in-page via fetch() with variables {currentPage:1, pageSize:900, url:'watches', filters:{category_uid:{eq:'NA=='}}, sort:{}, sizeRanges:{}, cache_buster_store:'de_de', cache_buster_lang:'de-de'} and request headers lang=de-de, store=de_de (matching the site's own request headers) to retrieve the entire catalog in one authoritative response rather than paging 24 items at a time.

collectionPath: 1. Opened https://www.longines.com/de/watches in an isolated browser context (isolatedContext=longines-de-market) separate from other in-progress market subagents' contexts/pages.
2. Accepted the site's cookie/consent dialog to unblock further interaction.

3. Read the rendered PLP: heading '804 Produkte', a 'Nur auf Lager' (in-stock only) toggle left OFF (default, so out-of-stock/backorder items with public prices remain included), and a 'Mehr Ergebnisse anzeigen' load-more control with progressbar text '24 items seen and 804 in total'.

4. Clicked 'Mehr Ergebnisse anzeigen' once to force the page to make its real paginated GraphQL ProductList request (URL changed client-side to ?page=2) and captured that exact request/response via list_network_requests + get_network_request.

5. Replayed the captured ProductList GraphQL query via evaluate_script/fetch() with pageSize=900 and currentPage=1, first without locale headers (returned English/GBP data - rejected, not used) and then with headers lang=de-de/store=de_de matching the original captured request (returned German/EUR data with total_count=804, items.length=804 - used as the authoritative dataset).

stopEvidence.matchesRenderedPlpHeading: 804 Produkte (confirmed both at initial page load and via the GraphQL total_count field)
stopEvidence.reasoning: pageSize (900) exceeds total_count (804); the API returned page_info.current_page=1 with all 804 items in the single response and total_count===items.length, so there is no further page/cursor to fetch. No infinite-scroll or DOM-only completeness signal was relied upon; the stop condition is the structured API's own total_count field matching the returned item count, cross-checked against the independently-rendered PLP heading text observed before any API replay.

conflictsFound: None. Each SKU appeared exactly once in the ProductList response.

attempts.method: In-page fetch() replay of captured ProductList GraphQL query, pageSize=900, currentPage=1, NO custom lang/store headers
attempts.result: HTTP 200, total_count=806, currency=GBP, category names in English -- locale resolved incorrectly (fell back to a prior session/geo default, not the German store view). NOT used for official data.
attempts.discardedReason: Locale/currency did not match the German market being collected; superseded by attempt 2.

attempts.method: Same fetch() replay, this time with request headers lang=de-de and store=de_de matching the original browser-issued request's headers
attempts.result: HTTP 200, total_count=804, currency=EUR, category names in German (e.g. 'Uhren', 'HYDROCONQUEST'), prices in German number format (comma decimal, e.g. '2.550,00 €'). Used as the sole authoritative dataset for all official data below.

priceFormatNote: German de-DE price strings use a comma as the decimal separator and a period as the thousands separator (e.g. '2.550,00 €' = two thousand five hundred fifty euros). The GraphQL base_price.value field returns this same amount as a plain integer number of whole euros (e.g. 2550), with zero fractional/cent components across all 804 items (verified programmatically), so it was used directly as the schema's integer price without any string parsing, multiplication, or rounding.
collectionsNote: The 31 collection slugs derived from each item's preferred_category.url_path last path segment exactly match the 31 distinct collectionId values already present in data/catalog/longines-catalog.json (no extra, none missing).
